title: Polygon Perimeter From Coordinates: Boundary
description: Compute the boundary length of a coordinate polygon with Polygon Perimeter From Coordinates — geodesic edge sums in miles and kilometres. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, the four Midtown Manhattan corners (40.7580, −73.9855 and around) make a boundary of 5.28 km — 3.28 miles of fence, path or edging, summed edge by edge on the sphere.
quick_answer: Polygon Perimeter From Coordinates computes the total boundary length of a polygon given by latitude/longitude corners, summing great-circle distances edge by edge and closing the ring automatically. Paste the corners in boundary order and read the perimeter in kilometres, miles and metres — for fencing, edging, paths and boundaries.

Anything that follows the boundary — a trail loop, a service run, a security patrol route — is a perimeter with a job title.
Deeds and listings quote perimeters from older surveys; the corners' own sum is the modern second opinion.
A closed course drawn on the map gets its true lap distance from its corners, geodesically summed.
Sides of 1.306, 1.334, 1.305 and 1.334 km sum to 5.279 km (3.28 mi). Opposite sides differ slightly — longitude edges ride converging meridians, and the sphere keeps the receipts.
A river boundary approximated by 6 corners under-measures the bends; 60 corners hug them. Perimeter grows toward the truth as corners multiply — coastlines taught us this humility.

faq: Does the tool close the polygon automatically?
Yes — the final edge from the last corner back to the first is included in the total. Do not repeat the first point.
What if my corners are out of order?
The sum follows the order given — a scrambled order measures a zigzag star, not your boundary. Walk the fence in the list as you would on foot.
Great-circle chords between your corners. Terrain, bends between corners and paths that wander all run longer in reality.
Kilometres, miles and metres are all reported — buy materials in whichever your supplier speaks.
A shape with a gap in its boundary?
Model the gap as part of the ring (the boundary still closes mathematically); for materials, subtract the gap's own length afterwards.
Geodesic edges are effectively exact for this purpose; the total's honesty is set by your corners' placement, not the arithmetic.
